provenance.note: A soft woodblock, the hand of the slow conversation (his ear, 10-17: the hand read as a clap, too stiff and striking for a sparse bell space; "some softer woodblock maybe better"). Built as a tuned wooden tok rather than a burst through a resonator: the membrane builder's head at 560 Hz (the record's woodblock rings 1400 and 2360) with a mode at 1.58 dying in 30 ms and a fall of 10 dB in 45 ms, a body under a 2 kHz lowpass and almost no hand on it, so it is round and has no click; a six-millisecond attack, so the strike has no edge, and a third of it to the room. (A noise burst through a resonator narrow enough to be round rang a different level at each sample rate and on each variant: the burst's few cycles in band are a die.)
